newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Probe says completes Siberian buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Probe says completes Siberian buy.

text.p: Probe Resources NL, relisted on the Australian Stock Exchange on Monday, said it has completed the acquisition of 50 percent of the West Siberian Mokhtikovskoye oilfield, which it said was producing from its first six wells at a higher than expected 1,500 barrels of oil per day.
Probe said it completed the acquisition of Irish company Minpetro Global Resources Ltd, which holds a 50 percent participating interest in the field, last week.

"The final acquisition and commissioning of the 48 million-plus barrel oilfield follows the recent over-subscribed closure of Probe's capital raising via the issue of 27.5 million Probe shares at 1O cents each, which raised A$2.76 million," Probe said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange.

It said the Mokhtikovskoye oilfield had current proven recoverable reserves of 26.5 million barrels, proven and probable recoverable reserves of 47.86 million barrels - enough for a production life of 33 years - and proven, probable and possible reserves totalling just under 70 million barrels.

The Russian operator and 50 percent partner, Siboil, had confirmed the completion of the first six development wells in September and that production is running at 1,500 barrels a day, well in excess of the development schedule, Probe said.
Probe also announced it had appointed new directors Marvin Billett, Dato Omar, Yuri Loganov, Dr Felix Lip, Adama Toungara and Mike Farrall.
Paul Byrne remains joint managing director with Michael Farrall, who will manage the petroleum side of Probe's operations. Peter Greenland and Don Royal have resigned.
Probe shares were trading at 8.5 cents on Monday compared with 12 cents on March 5, the last trade before the company was was delisted following a reorganisation.
